title: Japan scrambles fighter jets after Russian aircraft breach airspace amid rising Pacific tensions
text:
The incursion preceded a Quad warning against destabilizing actions, and officials told Fox News the USS George Washington was headed to the Pacific region

Russia unleashes missiles in massive Pacific war games

More than 13,000 troops and dozens of ships, submarines and aircraft take part in Russian naval drills across the Sea of Japan, Sea of Okhotsk and Northwest Pacific. (Credit: East2West)

Japan scrambled fighter jets early Tuesday after two suspected Russian aircraft entered Japanese airspace, prompting a rapid military response ahead of Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's warning of rising global instability during the Quad Leaders’ Summit in Manila.

Hours later, President Donald Trump had also joined Takaichi, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese at the summit, where the leaders voiced opposition to actions threatening regional peace and stability.

"We strongly oppose any destabilizing or unilateral actions that seek to change the status quo, including by force or coercion, which escalate tensions and undermine regional peace and stability," the leaders said in a joint statement later released by the White House.

TRUMP KICKS OFF HIGH-STAKES ASIA TRIP WITH XI, PUTIN MEETINGS LOOMING ON WORLD STAGE

Japan scrambled fighter jets after two suspected Russian aircraft entered Japanese airspace, prompting a rapid military response. (Aviation-images.com/Universal Images Group via Getty Images)

On Wednesday, two U.S. military officials confirmed to Fox News that the aircraft carrier USS George Washington was departing the Middle East for the Pacific.

Sen. Mazie Hirono, D-Hawaii, questioned acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao Tuesday about the lack of aircraft carriers in the Pacific, noting that three carrier strike groups had been deployed to the Middle East.

"There are none in the Indo-Pacific area when we are looking at China, not to mention North Korea and especially what China may have in mind," Hirono said.

"See, this is stretching and stressing our resources. You can't take away the strike group out of the Indo-Pacific."

The Russian aircraft entered Japanese airspace northwest of Okinoshima, an island in southwestern Japan's Fukuoka Prefecture, at about 4:07 a.m. local time Nov. 17, according to Japan's Defense Ministry.

Fighter jets from the Japan Air Self-Defense Force's Western Air Defense Force were scrambled to issue warnings and take other measures, the ministry said in a statement posted on X.

The first suspected Russian aircraft entered Japanese airspace at approximately 4:07 a.m. and remained for three minutes.

A second aircraft entered the same area at approximately 4:09 a.m. and departed three minutes later.

THREE MANILA MOMENTS THAT GIVE TRUMP MOMENTUM GOING INTO TALKS WITH CHINA

U.S. President Donald Trump, second from right, poses for photos with Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, left; Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, second left; and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese as they take part in a meeting of the Quad group at the Solaire Resort on the sidelines of the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations Summit in Manila Nov. 17, 2026. (Mandel Ngan/AFP via Getty Images)

Japan's Defense Ministry said the aircraft traveled through the Tsushima Strait and passed between Japan's Yonaguni Island and Taiwan before continuing into the Pacific Ocean.

"In response, the Self-Defense Forces scrambled fighter jets from the Japan Air Self-Defense Force’s Western Air Defense Force to issue notifications and warnings and take other measures," the Ministry of Defense said.

Japanese Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi said Tokyo lodged a strong protest with Moscow and demanded measures to prevent further airspace violations.

The incidents "not only constitute a grave infringement upon Japan’s sovereignty but also pose a threat to our security. They are entirely unacceptable," Koizumi said.

This came as Takaichi warned of growing instability in the international order and promised a bigger role for Japan in maintaining regional security.

CHINA, RUSSIA, IRAN AND NORTH KOREA FORM 'AXIS OF AGGRESSORS' THAT COULD OVERWHELM US, BOOK WARNS

Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi speaks during a news conference at the prime minister's office in Tokyo Oct. 21, 2025. (Eugene Hoshiko)

"While the international order is experiencing a period of great instability, Japan will play a more proactive role," Takaichi said during the Association of Southeast Asian Nations summit in Manila.

Takaichi emphasized Japan's commitment to maintaining an international order based on freedom, openness and the rule of law while strengthening cooperation with Southeast Asian nations.

"Our countries are the four corners of a free, open, stable and prosperous Indo-Pacific," Trump had also said ahead of the Quad meeting.

The leaders had expressed "grave concerns" about economic coercion, including arbitrary export restrictions, and outlined plans for a joint military exercise involving maritime patrol aircraft in 2027.

KIM JONG UN'S NUCLEAR BUILDUP SPARKS 'SERIOUS CONCERN' AHEAD OF TRUMP-XI-PUTIN SUMMIT

An F-35C stealth jet sits on the deck of the USS Carl Vinson in the Western Pacific, south of Japan. (Reuters/Tim Kelly)

The airspace incursion comes amid broader security concerns across the Indo-Pacific, where Japan and its regional partners have increasingly monitored Russian and Chinese military activity.

On Tuesday, South Korea’s air force also scrambled fighter jets as multiple Russian military aircraft had entered the country’s air defense identification zone, according to the Ministry of National Defense.

Otherwise, Japan's relations with Moscow have deteriorated since Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022, with Tokyo joining Western allies in imposing sanctions on the Kremlin.

The two countries are also locked in a decades-old territorial dispute over islands north of Japan's northernmost main island of Hokkaido. Russia administers the islands, which Japan claims as its Northern Territories.

Japan previously scrambled fighter jets in 2024 after a Russian military patrol aircraft entered Japanese airspace near Hokkaido three times.

Emma Bussey is a breaking news writer for Fox News Digital. Before joining Fox, she worked at The Telegraph with the U.S. overnight team, across desks including foreign, politics, news, sport and culture.
